brief.title: PC game storefronts that periodically let users permanently add normally-paid games for free
brief.scope: free-to-keep giveaways and paid-to-free conversions on PC storefronts. Excludes always-F2P games, demos, trials, playtests, DLC, and subscription-lending (unless noted).

summary: Six source categories: Steam, Epic Games Store, GOG, Amazon Prime Gaming (now Amazon Luna), itch.io, and community aggregators. The most reliable machine-readable feed is Epic's public freeGamesPromotions API. No store's raw 'free' filter can distinguish a temporary free-to-keep giveaway from a permanently-F2P game or a demo; programmatic detection requires tracking price/is_free change over time, or consuming curated community feeds.

sources.name: Steam
event_types: free-to-keep giveaways (publisher sets paid game to 100% off for a limited window; claim = keep forever)
permanent paid-to-free conversions (developer flips game to F2P)

access_methods.name: store search with price=0
access_methods.note: Heavily polluted with F2P and demos (~2,656 results)

access_methods.name: appdetails API (no key)
access_methods.note: Returns data.is_free (bool) and data.price_overview (omitted when free). Verified live.

access_methods.name: SteamDB upcoming/free
access_methods.note: Curated free-to-keep + free-weekend tracking with expiry. Some pages anti-bot/JS-rendered, need browser.

sources.signal_presented_as: price = $0 / 'Free' with a limited-time offer note (giveaway); is_free=true with no price_overview (conversion or F2P)
sources.update_cadence: Irregular: publisher-driven giveaways (multiple/week at peak sales, sometimes zero); permanent conversions sporadic (a few/month)
sources.detection_pitfall: is_free=true is indistinguishable between native F2P (Apex Legends verified) and converted game (Crusader Kings II verified). Must track False->True flip over time or use a curated list.

sources.name: Epic Games Store
event_types: weekly free-to-keep giveaway (1-2 games every Thursday since Dec 2018)

access_methods.name: official free games page
access_methods.note: Shows current + upcoming weeks; mixes giveaway with F2P and demo carousels on one DOM

access_methods.name: official public JSON API (no auth, verified live)

sources.signal_presented_as: 'Free Giveaway' header + struck original price; price=0 with a promotional offer block
sources.update_cadence: Weekly, deterministic: Thursday ~15:00 UTC, expires following Thursday; upcoming week usually pre-revealed
sources.free_detection_field: freeGamesPromotions JSON: promotionalOffers blocks with discountPercentage=0 on offerType=BASE_GAME
sources.detection_pitfall: F2P titles (Fortnite, Apex, etc.) have no promotionalOffers block; demos/trials/playtests share the page and must be excluded by offerType + title tokens.

sources.name: GOG
event_types: permanent 'always free' collection (never paid; ~12,545 DRM-free titles)
limited 48-hour giveaways during major sales/campaigns (e.g., Freedom to Buy Aug 2025 gave 13 titles; Nexus: The Jupiter Incident Jul 2026)

access_methods.name: catalog API (public, verified live)
access_methods.note: Returns permanently-free bucket (200 pages/10,000 shown); does NOT expose time-limited giveaways

access_methods.name: free collection page
access_methods.note: JS-rendered with client-side templating; use browser or catalog API

sources.signal_presented_as: price = 0 in catalog API (permanent bucket); giveaways announced via news/banners
sources.update_cadence: Permanent bucket stable; giveaways sporadic (a few per major sale, 48h windows)
sources.free_detection_field: catalog price=free (but mostly permanently-free, so giveaway events need gg.deals/r-gog)
sources.detection_pitfall: The free bucket is dominated by always-free titles; time-limited giveaways are not cleanly exposed in the catalog API.

sources.name: Amazon Prime Gaming / Amazon Luna
event_types: ~12 free PC games/month for active Prime subscribers, released in weekly batches
claims are codes/rewards that expire (end of month); redeemed games kept forever
also in-game bundles/loot and Luna cloud-streaming titles

access_methods.name: claims home
access_methods.note: Auth required; needs active Prime subscription

sources.signal_presented_as: 'Claim' reward card on the claims page; code with expiry
sources.free_detection_field: auth-gated; no stable public JSON feed
sources.detection_pitfall: Requires active paid subscription + credentials for headless access; no clean public API.

sources.name: itch.io
event_types: creator-initiated 100%-off sales making a normally-paid game temporarily free
creators may also run permanent 100% offers or long-duration sales

access_methods.name: creator sales docs
access_methods.note: 'You can set the rate to 100% if you want your content to be temporarily free.'

sources.detection_pitfall: No reliable machine-visible flag distinguishing always-free/PWYW from 'was paid and now temporarily free'; needs polling + price history.

sources.name: Community Aggregators (recommended machine-readable layer)
event_types: curated free-to-keep giveaways across all stores with expiry metadata

access_methods.name: r/FreeGameFindings
access_methods.note: ~430k members; flairs include 'previously given', 'f2p to paid', 'tasks'; accessible via .json or official API

access_methods.name: freeToKeep.gg
access_methods.note: Fetches official store feeds server-side, ~1 min cache; covers Steam/Epic/GOG/Prime/Stove + bundles

sources.signal_presented_as: curated listing with expiry / 'free to keep' labels
sources.detection_pitfall: Requires trusting community curation; some entries are subscription/task-gated.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Free != free-to-keep
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Price 0 or 'Free' badge is necessary-but-not-sufficient. Exclude always-F2P games (Fortnite, Apex, LoL, PoE, Warframe, etc.) that were never paid.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Cannot distinguish F2P vs converted from one snapshot (Steam)
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Verified: Apex Legends (F2P) and Crusader Kings II (converted to free) both return is_free=true with no price_overview. Track is_free/price False->True flip over time, or use a curated list.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Demos / playtests / betas / prologues / showcases
filtering_pitfalls.detail: e.g. Onimusha Demo, Detroit: Become Human Demo, Far Cry 6 FREE Trial, HITMAN WOA Free Demo, Lords of the Fallen Friend's Pass. Filter by offerType and title tokens (Demo/Trial/Playtest/Beta/Prologue/Showcase/Benchmark/Testing) and by base-game price.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Trials / Free Weekend / 'Play Free' (not permanent)
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Free weekends and trials revert to paid; distinguish 'keep' (Add to Library/Add to Account) from 'play' (temporary access) UI and expiry semantics.

filtering_pitfalls.title: DLC / add-ons / Starter Editions mislabeled as games
filtering_pitfalls.detail: e.g. Epic 'Lost Explorers' Swords Pack' DLC or a free 'Starter Edition'. Filter to BASE_GAME product types; drop ADD_ON/DLC/starter.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Bundles / compilations
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Epic offerType=BUNDLE (e.g. Tomb Raider I-III Remastered) is a legit giveaway but a bundle, not a single game; decide scope.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Pay-what-you-want / always-free itch titles
filtering_pitfalls.detail: No flag for 'became free recently'; requires price-history polling.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Region / currency variance
filtering_pitfalls.detail: A title may be free in one country but not another; pass explicit cc=/country= and note region.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Already-owned masking
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Authenticated accounts won't re-show price 0 for titles already owned; don't infer 'no longer free' from an account that owns the game. Query unauthenticated or track by entitlement.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Delisting giveaways
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Some games are made free right before permanent removal (e.g. MOUTHOLE). Real free-to-keep events but may be short-lived; mark as delisting-edge.

filtering_pitfalls.title: Subscription / task gating
filtering_pitfalls.detail: Prime Gaming requires an active paid sub; some giveaways require task completion. Decide scope before filtering.

recommendations: Primary automated feed: Epic freeGamesPromotions API (free, no auth, structured, deterministic weekly). Filter discountPercentage==0 + offerType==BASE_GAME + exclude demo/trial tokens.
Cross-store coverage: poll r/FreeGameFindings JSON + gg.deals freebies + SteamDB /upcoming/free/ + freeToKeep.gg to catch Steam/GOG/Prime/itch giveaways with no clean store API.
Steam paid-to-free detection: persist appdetails.is_free + price_overview per appid over time; False->True flip = permanent conversion. Cross-check SteamDB.
Maintain an exclusion blocklist: native-F2P anchors + DLC/Starter/Bundle/PE offer types + demo/trial title regex.
Prime Gaming: requires auth + active sub; use browser automation against luna.amazon.com/claims/home with user creds, or rely on aggregators.
itch.io: only practical via on-sale page polling + price diffing; lowest automation value.
open_questions: No single official cross-store free-to-keep API exists; a robust tracker must fuse 2-4 sources.
Prime Gaming has no stable public JSON feed; the old gamesdb.prime.amazon.com endpoint is unofficial and fragile.
SteamDB scraping is blocked from plain HTTP on some pages (JS/anti-bot); confirm a browser-based fetch if SteamDB is used as the Steam source of truth.
itch.io 'paid but temporarily free' has no programmatic differentiator; needs polling-based history.
Some giveaways are subscription/task-gated; decide scope before building the filter.
